messages:
alex: Seeing a weird p99 jump out of FRA POP starting ~08:13 UTC, sustained for ~12m. p50 fine, p95 up ~40ms, p99 +220ms. Not obvious from infra graphs.
maya: Ah ok. Any correlation with kernel selection logs or batch sizes? :thinking:
alex: Checked autoscaler and host utilization — GPU load steady. CPU on the host had spikes in iowait and some procsteal. Also noticed frequent kernel fallback entries in runtime logs:
alex: ```
runtime: kernel_select: chosen=fast_attention_quant, fallback=fast_attention_float, reason=kernel_probe_mismatch
runtime: kvcache: miss_rate=0.12, eviction=low
``` 
benji: procsteal usually points to noisy VM on same host (hypervisor scheduling). Which cloud/instance type?
alex: Running on fra-pop dedicated pool (g4dn-style equivalent). Host metric shows a burst of context_switches and rcu stalls at the same window.
lia: Can you grep perf samples? If kernel selection probes are oscillating that could explain jitter while the runtime probes different instruction paths.
alex: Ran a quick perf capture at 08:20 — shared snippet:
alex: ```
# perf top sample
  18.2%  runtime_bin  [.] build_kv_snapshot
  12.5%  runtime_bin  [.] kernel_probe_fast_attn
  9.1%   kernel       [k] schedule
  7.8%   runtime_bin  [.] apply_attention_kernel
```
maya: Interesting, build_kv_snapshot high suggests KV cache work is spiking for some requests and blocking other tasks.
benji: Any change in request distribution? Longer context windows or batch skew?
alex: No prod config change. Trace shows many short requests but a subset with long context causing the server to allocate larger KV pages and probe kernels for quantized path.
devon: Do we have recent changes to kernel probing heuristic? I merged a small change last week that relaxes the cold-start probe timeout — could cause more probe attempts at runtime.
maya: Which commit? link?
devon: commit 9f3a2c4 — it defers marking kernel unstable until 3 probes instead of 1.
lia: That could cause longer windows where the runtime repeatedly attempts the newer kernel on some sequences, incurring extra CPU work and latency. If noisy neighbor causes occasional preemption, probes may fail and fallback, toggling kernels.
alex: Workaround I tried: bumping probe backoff and increasing probe interval reduced oscillation. After that p99 dropped back to baseline.
benji: Good to know. We should still root-cause procsteal — cloud reported a maintenance noise on the FRA cluster at the time? I see a peering update event 08:10 that coincides.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1457 — FRA POP latency spike. https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-1457
maya: Suggest action items:
- short: revert or add conservative backoff to kernel probe (devon)
- medium: add KV snapshot throttling for long-context requests to avoid blocking short ones (alex/lia)
- infra: ask cloud to surface noisy host/eviction causes (benji)
- observability: add a metric for kernel_probe_attempts and kernel_switch_count (maya)
devon: I'll open a PR to gate the probe frequency and add a flag to disable aggressive probing per-pop. Targeting a hotfix roll by EOD.
alex: Patch applied to FRA rollout, monitoring now. p99 returning to normal after ~6m.
lia: For longer term, we should instrument the runtime to emit a probe-state timeline per request id so we can correlate probe transitions with latency spikes.
benji: Also consider isolating latency-sensitive routes onto separate hosts or cgroups to avoid procsteal from noisy tenants.
maya: Noted. I'll file follow-ups and add the new metrics to the perf dashboard.
alex: Thanks all — closing thread once postmortem doc is up. :thumbsup:
